COS-80.10-Q1#X.why: Withheld: user saw only the withholding notice. None of the key's fee ($0.45/lb, min $288, so $900), payment method or advance-deposit elements was delivered, although 80.10 was in the evidence.

COS-80.10-Q1#Y.why: Generic 'not enough information' decline. The key's fee, payment-method and advance-deposit elements are all missing, although 80.10 was in the evidence.

COS-80.31-Q1#1.why: Generic decline. The three findings FDA must make and the certificate contents (lot number, certified statement) are missing, although 80.31 was in the evidence.

COS-80.37-Q1#1.why: Generic decline. The storage, control and marking requirements of 80.37(a)-(c) are missing; 80.37 was not in the evidence.

COS-80.38-Q1#1.why: Generic decline. The lot-number labeling and storage-until-packaged requirements of 80.38(a)-(b) are missing; 80.38 was not in the evidence.

COS-81.30-Q1#X.why: Decline with a stray [1] marker pointing to an unrelated (real) lead-in-cosmetics draft guidance. The 81.30(r) answer (certificates cancelled, so the lots can't be used) is missing; 81.30 was not in the evidence.

COS-81.30-Q1#Y.why: Generic decline. The 81.30(r) answer (certificates cancelled for externally applied use after July 15, 1988, so no) is missing; 81.30 was not in the evidence.

COS-82.6-Q1#1.why: Generic decline. The 82.6(a)(1)-(3) conditions, including the sodium benzoate 1/10 of 1 percent allowance, are missing, although 82.6 was in the evidence.

COS-82.50-Q1#X.why: Generic decline. The 82.50 answer (certifiable for food, drugs and cosmetics if it meets 82.5 and the subpart specifications) is missing; 82.50 was not in the evidence.

COS-82.50-Q1#Y.why: Correctly says the batch may be used in cosmetics if it meets 82.5 and the subpart specifications, but names 82.1050 and 82.2050 (the subpart C/D certification sections) as governing, so ce=0. Never cites 82.50, omits that cosmetic use is governed by the color's listing and restrictions, and ends with a contradictory 'not enough information' line.

COS-82.101-Q1#1.why: Correctly states that FD&C Blue No. 1 must conform to 74.101(a)(1) and (b), cited to 82.101; every other marker also matches its quoted text. The 82.5 condition is cut off at 'unless:' with no lead, arsenic or heavy-metal limits, 82.50 is not surfaced, and there are blank items and an irrelevant mixture (82.6(a)) fragment.

COS-82.203-Q1#1.why: Correctly states that FD&C Green No. 3 must conform to 74.203(a)(1) and (b), correctly cited to 82.203. It omits 82.50 and the 82.5 general specifications (lead, arsenic, heavy metals), which could mislead the user into thinking 74.203 is the whole requirement.

COS-82.304-Q1#1.why: Gives the external-use restriction and the 74.1304(a)(1) and (b) conformity, both cited to 82.304 (but mislabels the color as 'D&C Red No. 4'). The 82.5(a) impurity clause is garbled into an inverted statement ('shall be certified unless it is free from impurities'). The 82.5 lead and arsenic limits and 82.50 are missing, and there are fragments plus an irrelevant D&C Blue No. 4 line.

COS-82.1104-Q1#1.why: Generic decline. The key's 'no' is missing: no mention of the external-use-only restriction, that lips are excluded under 70.3(v), or the 74.1104 specifications. Neither 82.1104 nor 70.3 was in the evidence.

COS-82.1205-Q1#1.why: Accurately quotes the single sentence of 82.1205 (conform to 74.1205(a)(1) and (b)(2)), correctly cited. It does not state outright that there is no use restriction or limit, and it omits the 82.1050 drugs-and-cosmetics-only certification condition with 82.5.
